grounding.states: large eggs dropped into boiling water: about 12 minutes gives a fully hard-boiled egg; 10 minutes is firm but may be slightly soft in the center
grounding.from: Healthline says 12 to 13 minutes gives fully hard-boiled eggs that are not over-cooked. At 10 minutes, the eggs are mostly cooked through but slightly soft in the center.

grounding.states: past about 14-15 minutes the eggs turn rubbery or dry
grounding.from: Past about 14–15 minutes the eggs turn rubbery or dry.

value.answer: For large eggs dropped into boiling water, go about 12 minutes for a fully set yolk. 10 minutes is firm but can be a bit soft in the middle, and past 14 or 15 minutes the whites get rubbery and the yolk dry. Put them in cold water after to stop the cooking.
